sampling_model.design: A binary instrument \(Z\) randomized conditionally on finite-support \(X\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \((X,Z,D,V)\) for the finite-sample coverage theorem; identification itself is a population-law statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary received treatment \(D=D_Z\) with all four compliance types permitted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed arm-state masses \(q\) are multinomial functionals; the baseline confidence surface projects a simultaneous primitive region and does not require a smooth endpoint estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under conditional IV restrictions, treatment monotonicity, conditional-first-stage support, and a covariate-dependent one-sided selection direction, Dong--Heiler analyze an intensive-margin complier mean. The accepted CausalSmith pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport_v1 result already supplies the branch-free finite-ordinal partial-transport projection, threshold cuts, full-law lifting, sharp endpoints, and sparse computation at this no-defier boundary; the present theorem recovers that boundary at zero budgets and extends only the positive-budget joint-violation problem.
Expands sharp ordinal-benefit bounds to observational settings and imperfect randomized trials.
Derives uniformly sharp bounds for marginal treatment effects among always-observed individuals in a latent-index treatment model, with tighter bounds under monotone sample selection.
Derives nonparametric average-effect bounds under sample selection and noncompliance.
Derives breakdown frontiers for average effects and the proportion benefiting under two assumption relaxations.
Derives LATE and average-effect bounds under joint relaxations of independence and monotonicity.
Constructs an output-sensitive polyhedral decomposition for sufficient-matrix multiparametric complementarity problems.
Uses lexicographic perturbation to obtain a unique continuous optimizer over nonoverlapping regions.
Its confidence interval procedure for the fraction benefiting is pointwise consistent.
Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated-projection confidence intervals.
Provides uniform asymptotic inference using randomly perturbed linear-program value functions.

body.tldr: With randomized binary assignment, endogenous receipt, and an ordinal outcome observed only after post-treatment selection, the positive defier and selection-minority budgets yield an exact finite union of orientation-specific rational threshold-cut polytopes, and every reduced point lifts to a compatible full law. Each branch, not the whole disjunctive problem, has \(O(mK)\) size. The scalar sharp set is an attained interval; finite all-bases charts label model infeasibility, model-feasible target emptiness, and target-nonempty endpoint formulas without extending \(L\) or \(U\) through \(H=0\). Radial reports distinguish model entry, target entry, and actual conclusion failure. At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), the construction recovers the branch-free partial-transport projection, ordinal cuts, full-law lift, sharp endpoints, and sparse threshold-flow computation already proved in the accepted CausalSmith paper \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\). The new extension is the positive-budget regime with unknown diagonal residuals and defiers, within-cell coexistence of opposing selection responses, a budget-coupled survivor mass, and an orientation-indexed union. Output-sensitive chart enumeration remains open.

project_justification.gap: The accepted CausalSmith paper \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\) already closes the no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection boundary with a branch-free partial-transport projection, ordinal threshold cuts, full-law lifting, sharp attained endpoints, and sparse linear-time threshold flow. Published selected-complier and ordinal-benefit analyses do not supply the positive-budget combination of treatment defiers, within-cell opposing selection responses, an aggregate minority-selection budget, and a survivor denominator that may be absent.
project_justification.niche: The remaining mathematical niche is therefore the joint-violation surface at positive \(\delta_D\) and \(\delta_S\): diagonal residuals and defier margins are unknown, both selection directions may coexist in each covariate cell, and survivor mass is coupled across cells by the minority budget. Target existence must be separated from both model feasibility and robustness.
project_justification.fill: The projection and reverse lift reduce compatible full laws exactly to a finite orientation-indexed union whose individual branches have \(O(mK)\) extended size. Attained endpoints, sparse full-law certificates, finite rational charts, closure-correct boundary labels, and exact radial critical-budget reports follow. At zero budgets the formulas specialize to, and explicitly credit, the accepted branch-free boundary result; no new zero-budget algorithm is claimed.

body.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith paper \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\), through \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval}\), \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:full-law-endpoint-attainment}\), and \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:linear-sparse-threshold-flow}\), already establishes the branch-free survivor-complier partial-transport projection, ordinal threshold cuts, full-law lifting, sharp attained endpoints, and sparse \(O(|\mathcal X|K)\) computation on the no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection boundary. That boundary is the finite-ordinal Dong--Heiler anchor under their conditional-first-stage and assignment-overlap support convention. The present result recovers it at \((0,0)\) and extends the model only at positive budgets, where defier residuals are unknown, opposing selection responses coexist within cells, survivor mass is coupled by an aggregate budget, and an orientation disjunction is unavoidable. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen study ordinal benefit without this post-treatment-selection denominator. Bartalotti, K\'edagni, and Possebom use a latent-index treatment rule and monotone-selection refinement that exclude the violations admitted here. Masten and Poirier motivate two-assumption conclusion frontiers, while Picchetti supplies a defier-share sensitivity coordinate; neither separates model entry, survivor-target entry, and conclusion failure. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski motivate symbolic parametric-optimization tools but do not deliver a degeneracy-safe output-sensitive enumerator for this disjunctive rational chart.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The proved symbolic construction is finite all-bases enumeration, including singular and lower-dimensional strata; it is not output-sensitive. Positive-budget \(O(mK)\) size holds per orientation branch only, and as many as \(2^m\) branches may remain. The early kill test must still reproduce the explicit binary surface, the opposite-orientation witness, and the vanishing-denominator example with exact equality and empty-target strata, endpoint full-law certificates, and an audit excluding hidden exponential rejected-basis work. Failure of that computational test does not affect the projection, pointwise endpoint, chart-existence, or radial-characterization theorems.
body.honest_scope: The note proves the ordinal-cut characterization, exact positive-budget full-law projection and lift, attained connected endpoints, sparse endpoint laws, finite rational charts with endpoints only on target-nonempty strata, closure-correct breakdown labels, exact radial entry and critical-budget reports, simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage, and the zero-budget reduction. The branch-free zero-budget projection, lifting, sharp endpoints, and sparse threshold-flow algorithm are credited to the accepted \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\) result and are recovered here rather than claimed as new. The \(O(mK)\) formulation bound is per orientation branch; no branch-free, polynomial, strongly polynomial, scalable, or output-sensitive positive-budget algorithm is claimed. Equality loci \(L=t\) are not called conclusion boundaries unless their closures meet both robust and target-nonempty nonrobust pieces. Pre-feasibility and pre-target portions of a radial path are not robustness. The output-sensitive degeneracy-safe enumerator, regular endpoint inference at ties, and empirical reanalysis remain outside scope.
